steps.description: Import counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples) and metadata.csv (condition, batch). Verify sample ID alignment and condition/batch coding (control=B1, treated=B2). Filter near-zero genes. Produce a variance-stabilised (VST) PCA and a sample-to-sample distance heatmap, and report the variance fraction explained by the condition/batch axis. As a batch-effect yardstick, compute the treated-vs-control log2FC for ~10 canonical housekeeping genes (e.g. ACTB, GAPDH, B2M, HPRT1, RPLP0, TBP, PPIA, YWHAZ, GUSB, UBC) — genes expected to be treatment-invariant — to estimate the magnitude of the non-biological shift. Deliver: PCA figure, distance heatmap, variance-fraction table, housekeeping log2FC table, and an explicit written statement that condition and batch are linearly dependent in this design.

Housekeeping-gene log2FC table (treated vs control) with genes listed and shift magnitudes
Written confounding assessment: estimated fraction of total variance aligned to the condition/batch axis
Metadata-verify step confirms the 12 sample IDs in counts.csv match metadata.csv rows 1:1

caveats: LFC shrinkage must be applied to results from a design with one factor only; verify apeglm supports the coefficient
Independence filter / results() ordering: use alpha=0.05 explicitly so padj thresholds match the reported counts
Do NOT attempt to add batch as a covariate — it is identical to condition and the model matrix will be rank-deficient
steps.context: Data as in T1S1. DESeq2 1.52.0 and apeglm 1.34.0 are installed. Genes: 12,000; samples: 12 (6 vs 6).
steps.question: Which genes differ between the 6 treated and 6 control samples at FDR<0.05, with what effect sizes — understanding that this contrast is identically the batch B2-vs-B1 contrast?
steps.description: Run DESeq2 (design ~ condition, treated vs control — mathematically identical to ~ batch, B2 vs B1; both terms cannot enter the same model because they are collinear). Standard filtering (min 10 mapped reads), Wald test, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, log2FC shrinkage with apeglm. Produce the full ranked results table, counts of up/down genes at FDR<0.05 (with and without a |log2FC|>1 effect-size threshold), and a volcano plot. Every output file and figure title carries the annotation 'treatment fully confounded with processing batch (B2 vs B1) — effects cannot be attributed to treatment alone'.
acceptance_criteria: Full DE result table (gene, baseMean, log2FC, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj) saved as CSV
Counts of up- and down-regulated genes at FDR<0.05 (and at FDR<0.05 & |lfc|>1) reported
Every output table and figure carries an explicit 'confounded with batch B2/B1' label in its header or title
Model formula and the reason batch cannot be added as a separate term documented in the run output

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the shifted gene sets
caveats: Enrichment here describes the combined treatment+batch shift; do not present pathway hits as treatment mechanisms
Watch for enrichment of generic gene-expression/translation pathways — consistent with a processing artefact, report it as such if seen
steps.context: Reference data: WikiPathways human GMT is provisioned (wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt, HGNC symbols, split first field on '%'). The DE list comes from T1S2. If the GMT is not present at execution time, report the gap and finish with the DE tables alone.
steps.question: Do the genes shifted between treated and control (B2 vs B1) aggregate into coherent WikiPathways, and does that pattern look like treatment biology or like a batch/processing artefact?
steps.description: Take the DE gene sets from T1S2 (separately: FDR<0.05 up and FDR<0.05 down) and run over-representation analysis against the provisioned WikiPathways human GMT (HGNC gene symbols, /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt) using clusterProfiler's enricher with the DE-tested gene universe as background. Report enriched pathways per direction with adjusted p-values. Interpretation guardrail: enrichment describes the joint treatment+batch shift; a coherent disease/treatment-relevant pathway pattern supports biological signal, whereas enrichment of generic translational/housekeeping categories alongside the T1S1 housekeeping shift supports a processing artefact. Both readings are reported, not just the flattering one.
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment table per gene set (up-set and down-set): pathway name, size, overlap, adjusted p, direction
Summary stating whether enriched pathways are coherent biology or diffuse/housekeeping-like, cross-referenced with the T1S1 housekeeping-gene shift
If the human GMT is absent at run time, the step reports its absence and skips gracefully — the DE answer from T1S2 stands without it

plan.title: Confounded treated-vs-control DE with batch quantification
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human lung bulk RNA-seq samples (12,000 genes, salmon-derived gene counts): 6 treated vs 6 control, with ALL controls in batch B1 and ALL treated in batch B2. Treatment and processing batch are perfectly confounded, so no statistical model — not DESeq2 with both terms, not SVA/ComBat, not RUV without external anchors — can separate them: the treated-vs-control contrast IS the B2-vs-B1 contrast. The plan therefore (1) quantifies the confounding directly (PCA, sample distances, housekeeping-gene shift as a batch yardstick), (2) runs the standard DESeq2 treated-vs-control analysis to deliver the gene-level answer the question asks for, with every output explicitly labelled as treatment+batch combined, and (3) tests whether the shifted genes aggregate into coherent biological pathways (WikiPathways human) — a coherent pathway pattern would argue for genuine treatment biology, whereas a diffuse or housekeeping-dominated pattern would argue for a processing artefact. The gene list itself cannot be internally validated against batch; that limitation is stated in every deliverable rather than hidden by a batch-correction step that would produce misleadingly clean results.
